caption: Kar. 64. Altar (Kar. Cem., Pl. 17. No. 7098)
reading: wosi : a (2)soreyi : qo : (3)reqorelowi [.][.]e?tmdeqe(4)se : qoretkrqowi : arkiye : (5)tedḫlebkwi : ñwkr : teri(6)kelebkwi : (7)ato [.](8)ẖe pso(9)ẖebḫte : (10)at : mẖe[.] psḫrbḫte : (11)ḫmlol pẖolbḫte : pese(12)tolyetmdelebkwi : (13)mlidw(14)seqowi (15)semlowi : (16)mitleye : ted(17)ḫlowi : nobtr : (18)terikelowi : a(19)ḫmẖe : p(20)soẖte : (21)at : mẖe : psḫr(22)kete : ḫmlol pẖo(23)lkete : wosi a(24)soreyi :
notes: 24 numbered lines, set in 11 rows; where a row holds two blocks the right block is read first (line numbers confirm). 'qo' and 'q' are the slash + looped 3 (q form, as in the sign table); plain closed 3 after a slash is read s + o (so in soreyi, pso). Line 1: 'a' is S and a long-tailed 2 standing apart; the closing 'wosi a(24)soreyi' repeats the same opening. Line 3: the sign after r (small S-form) read e?; the sign before the hatching is an x-like mark read i?; hatching about two signs wide, then a partly hatched 9-like sign read e? (cf. yetmde in line 12). Line 2/3 'qorel?krqowi': of the two S-like signs between r and k, the taller one read l?, could be e or the two together a (S + 2). Line 5 'tedḫlebkwi' and line 17 'tedḫlowi': the copy shows only one of e/l after ḫ (the lightning form l); no e is written. Line 6 first sign is a λ with a loop at the top: ñ? (could be d). Line 6 'kele?bkwi': l, then about one sign of hatching with a 9-like remnant, read e?. Line 7-8: after 'ato' about one sign hatched (m expected in ato mẖe). In the benedictions the curvy ɛ-topped long-tailed sign is read p, the flat Ʒ-topped one k. 3-shaped signs: closed 3 read s; 3 with a tail to the lower left read ẖ or m from the formula (mẖe) and marked ? elsewhere. Line 11 and 22: the sign between m and o is S-like, read l? (mlol), could be e; in line 22 the m is hatched over (m?). Line 13 first sign is a tailed 3 crossed by a stroke, read ẖ?. Line 14 'sesywi': plain 3 then three slashes, read s + y; s + o + y, or q + y are possible. Line 15 'seẖtewi': se, a tailed 3, then slash + ϟ with a bar, read te (could be o + l). Line 16 first sign is a tailed 3, m? (or ẖ). Line 17 the d is a ʌ with a long tail (could be n). Line 18-19 father's name 'nobtr': ℛ with long tail (n), slash (o), ν (b), dotted ϟ (t), ω (r). Line 21 'mẖl?': small S-form with a hook after ẖ, read l (could be e). Row 2 of the copy has no divider between lines 14 and 15 (two blocks).
check_notes: All 41 entries placed. Names table (p. 90) settles persons 1-3 and their parents; formulae A, B, C (parts a and b) agree with the copy except a(19): the copy has a c-shaped ḫ where formula A (table, 64 b) prints to (ato) - kept the copy. Line 5 tedḫlebkwi: copy shows one sign between ḫ and b where Index C prints tedḫelebkwi - kept, nothing added. Line 17 tedḫlowi has no entry and stays. Line 14: the copy draws three slashes before the looped 3; Griffith reads q + o (seqowi), the same two signs I had as s + y. Index C prints n (R form) for the father in nwkr, the names table prints ñ (λ form) as the copy does - kept ñ. Index C 'qo : qor(?)elowi' omits the re that the copy and the names table show - kept re. Line 3 '[.][.]e?tmdeqe(4)se' has no entry and stays as in step 1.

caption: Kar. 65. Stela
reading: wosi : soreyi : m (2)li wi temome qo(3)wi : ḫrye : tedḫe(4)lowi : skliye teri(5)kelowi : ato mḫe pso(6)ẖekete : atmḫe p(7)siḫrkete :
notes: 7 numbered lines in three rows, right block first in each row. Line 1 ends with a sign like 7/ℸ, read m. Line 2 begins with a curled S-form joined to the following 4, read l? (could be e). 'teẖ?ome': after te a tailed 3 then a short slash, read ẖ + o; the pair could also be q. 'qo(3)wi': slash slash + looped 3 = q + o. The divider before ḫrye is a single dot, written ' : '. 'ḫrye': the y is three slashes with the first one longer and set apart (could be o + y). 'skliye': closed 3 (s), flat-topped long-tailed k, hooked 4-form l, i, y, e; no divider before terikelowi, only a gap. Line 5 'ato?': the to (ب with dot) is hatched as damaged. Line 6-7 second benediction 'atm?ḫe': the sign between t and ḫ is a near-straight slash, read m (the ) form) from the formula, could be o. 'p(7)siḫr': visually 4 before 3, so s then i.
check_notes: All 13 entries placed. Names table and Index C give (mli)witemomeqowi: settles l, and the tailed 3 after te as m. Formula A table prints the first sign of mḫe in a form the typist took for ẖ; the copy has the ) form of m and Griffith's prose and Index C list Kar. 65 under mḫe - kept m. The single-dot divider before ḫrye has no entry and stays written ' : '.

caption: Kar. 66. Altar
labels: fault?, by line 3 (over the hatching at the start of the left block)
sic, by line 5 (over the dotted ϟ before the a-tail, start of the second benediction)
reading: wosi : (2)sore(3)se? : [.] smlbeqo(4)wi : ato mẖe : psiẖe(5)kete : at mẖe : psḫ(6)rkete :
notes: 6 numbered lines in two rows, right block first. The line number 2 stands over the divider after wosi. Line 3: after sore the copy has the se form (ʋ//), not 4 (i) — y + i (soreyi) would be expected; read se?. The hatching labelled 'fault?' is about two signs wide and written [.][.]; Griffith's label suggests a flaw in the stone, so possibly no signs are lost there. After it: tailed 3 (ẖ?), 3 with a dotted line below (s), small S-form (l?, could be e), ν (b), S (e), slash slash + looped 3 = qo, then (4)wi. Line 5: 'at?' is copied as a dotted ϟ (t) followed by the long tail of a, marked sic; read a + t (at mẖe), the a lacks its S part.
check_notes: All 7 entries placed. Names table gives [.](?)smlbeqowi: one lost sign (Griffith's ? over a small hatched block), then s, m, l - so the hatching labelled 'fault?' is one sign, and the two 3-shapes are s then m. Formula B: Griffith prints (a)t and calls the a a blunder (only its right stroke); written at. Line 3 sore(3)se? has no entry and stays as in step 1.
